subject.title: Support Azure Foundry GPT Realtime Talk via gateway relay

question: Should Azure Foundry Realtime Talk land first as a server-side API-key Gateway Relay path using the existing OpenAI provider fields, or wait for a broader Azure auth design that includes Entra/managed identity before any support is accepted?
rationale: The right implementation changes credential handling and Azure endpoint/redirect behavior, and automation cannot choose the security boundary or supported auth contract for maintainers.

options.title: API-key relay first
options.body: Land a narrow API-key-only Gateway Relay implementation with strict server-side credential handling, GA endpoint tests, docs, and live proof, then track Entra as follow-up.

options.title: Wait for full Azure auth
options.body: Hold implementation until API-key, Entra, managed identity, SecretRef, and redirect policy are designed together.

options.title: Plugin-only experiment
options.body: Keep core unchanged for now and ask for an external plugin/prototype until the Azure realtime API and quota story is proven.

recommendation.title: API-key relay first
recommendation.body: Land a narrow API-key-only Gateway Relay implementation with strict server-side credential handling, GA endpoint tests, docs, and live proof, then track Entra as follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: The open question is primarily an auth-provider and credential-boundary decision, and this person most recently changed realtime voice auth behavior.
